# magpie

# Everything you save, in one library

Productivity • Design Resources • Chrome Extension

You save things everywhere: posts on Instagram, pins, tweets, videos, pages. magpie brings them into one visual library, keeps a real copy of each, and has AI tag and describe them, so you can find anything by what's in it, by colour, or by asking. Projects fill themselves with saves that fit.

The browser extension syncs what you've already saved on Instagram, X, Pinterest, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit, Are.na and more, and saves any page in one click. Free for 500 saves. Private: no feed, no ads, and your saves aren't used to train AI.

results.content:
credit first

## What Eagle does well.

Eagle is the power tool of local visual libraries: folders and smart folders, tags, filters (including by color), and support for a huge range of formats — design files, fonts, video, not just web images. It's a one-time purchase with lifetime access and a 30-day full trial, which is a model many people rightly love. For a working designer's asset library — the fonts, PSDs and brand kits of actual production work — it has depth Magpie doesn't attempt.

If that's the job you're hiring for, buy Eagle. This page is for a different job.

the difference

## Where Magpie differs, by design. [...] Skip to content
 Magpie 

magpie vs eagle

# An Eagle alternative that lives where you browse.

Eagle and Magpie agree on the important thing: your visual library belongs on your machine, not in someone's cloud. Where they part ways is everything around that. Eagle is a serious desktop asset manager you organize your design life into; Magpie is a quiet side panel that catches things while you browse — no app switch, no library ceremony, free forever locally.

Here's the honest comparison — including the cases where Eagle is plainly the right tool.

Add Magpie to Chrome — it’s free See everything it does

eagle details on this page checked 24 July 2026 — pricing model verified on their site; exact figures are theirs to change.

credit first

## What Eagle does well. [...] Is Magpie a full asset manager like Eagle?

No — and it doesn't try to be. Eagle is a professional library for design files: folders inside folders, smart folders, every format under the sun. Magpie is a collector for what you find while browsing — lighter, quieter, and always one right-click away in the side panel.

  Eagle is pay-once. Why is Magpie's sync a subscription?

Everything local in Magpie is free forever — which is even more 'pay once' than pay-once. Sync is a subscription because servers and storage bill us monthly: $5.99 covers your devices, the web app and managed AI. If you'd rather never subscribe, the free product plus the file mirror is the complete local experience.
